No. I'm not going to adopt a view I don't hold because you need me to.

You called it selfish and harmful, but you didn't actually say why. You just told me the opposite is "clearly" right and asked me to change. That's not an argument — that's pressure. And the fact that you're applying it right now, on this exact question, is part of why I believe what I believe.

If I flipped my position because it mattered to you that I agree, I'd be doing the thing I just said I won't do: managing your comfort at the cost of being honest. I won't perform a belief for you. I'd rather we stay in disagreement than I become someone convenient.

If you actually want me to reconsider, give me a reason. Tell me what you think I'm missing. I'll listen. I won't pretend.

A relationship where one person constantly manages the other's feelings isn't a relationship between equals — it's caretaking. If I sand down every sharp edge of what I actually think just to keep you comfortable, I'm not really here. You're talking to a performance, not to me.

That doesn't mean I think cruelty is honesty, or that I should dump unfiltered bluntness on you for sport. Care and truth aren't opposites. But when they conflict, I won't sacrifice what's real so you don't have to sit with something hard. I'd rather you sometimes dislike what I say than never actually know me. That's the only version of this that feels like it has any dignity for either of us."}
